title: Janitor work at Bullock's while starting in music
summary: In Los Angeles he worked as a janitor at Bullock's and picked up few music jobs, as he was still learning.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: Day jobs: musicians working outside music

blocks.x: One question, too, when you got to Los Angeles, were you able to get right into music.
No.
Did you take other jobs?
I took other jobs.
Like what kind of jobs, if you don't mind telling us.
I don't mind telling you. You know where I was. Down at Bullock's Department Store, working.
What kind of work?
Anything I could do there, anything I could get to do.
Whatever they needed you on, you could do.
Yeah.
Was that like you had to do janitor work.
Yeah, janitor work, that's mostly what it was.
Maintenance, whatever.
Maintenance. Sure.
Now, was there any chance to move up to a better job at that point?
No, there wasn't no chance to move up to it, but as soon as I got well enough acquainted with the people and all, I said I'll get out of this place, and I got out of it too.
Then were you able to get into music?
Yeah, I got into music.
Began to get a few jobs, right?
Got a few jobs in music.

So did you have to go back and forth, you know what I mean, in other words, after you got into music, was it strong enough as far as salary to keep you playing all the time, or did you have to have another job?
Yeah, it wasn't strong enough. I couldn't play good enough.
You couldn't play good enough.
No, I couldn't play good enough at that point. I was busy trying to learn to play.
So, in other words, you were doing maybe a day job and a night job at the same time?
Yep.
So when did the -- might have been years later when you got to the point where you were --
Oh, years later, you might as well
get off of it because I can't tell you much about what happened.
Do you feel that you got that much better, you know, musically, which you should have.
Sure, sure.
